key_insight: Privileged Cross-modal Relational Distillation (PCRD) uses high-resolution 2D images during training to improve specimen-specific 3D microstructure reconstruction from lower-resolution volumetric images alone.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly high-resolution 3D imaging when characterizing carbon fiber-reinforced polymer microstructures.
method: Use scanning electron microscopy as the privileged training modality and micro-CT as the inference input.
Transfer spatial organization by matching similarity distributions around corresponding spatial anchors.
Distill relational information without directly aligning heterogeneous feature vectors.
evidence_signal: PCRD improved 2D reconstruction mAP by 1.66 percentage points over direct micro-CT training and matched 89.97% of reference fiber centerline length in independent synchrotron CT validation, versus 75.08% for the interpolated low-resolution volume.
watch_item: Training requires corresponding spatial anchors across modalities; robustness to imperfect correspondence and generalization beyond the demonstrated composite remain to be established.
paper_title: Learning from high-resolution 2D images to reconstruct 3D microstructures
